accepted.question_text: For the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB, which gradings by small finite abelian groups preserve the algebraic or coalgebraic structure? More concretely, for groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, and Z2 × Z2, classify the group actions or coactions that turn these paraparticle algebras into graded module algebras or graded module coalgebras.

evidence.quote: 1st Research Objective: The first problem we intend to investigate is the classification of the gradings induced on the paraparticle (co)algebras (especially on PBF and PFB algebras) by small order finite Abelian Groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, Z2 × Z2 etc. In other words, we intend to classify those group (co)actions which preserve the corresponding (co)algebra structures, turning thus the (co)algebras in CG-(co)module (co)algebras.

accepted.question_text: For each grading of the paraparticle algebras under consideration, what braided group structures are possible? Equivalently, determine the compatible bicharacters, universal R-matrices of the corresponding group Hopf algebras, and braidings on the associated module or comodule categories, and decide which of these choices support compatible graded algebra and coalgebra structures that actually produce a braided group.

evidence.quote: 2nd Research Objective: Further, for each of the above gradings we intend to classify the corresponding braided group structures. In other words, we will write down the possible bicharacters of the above groups or equivalently the possible R-matrices of the corresponding group Hopf algebras or equivalently the braidings of the corresponding Category CGM (or MCG) of modules (or comodules). For each one of these braidings, we aim to examine whether or not there are available compatible graded algebraic and coalgebraic structures suitable for producing a braided group.

accepted.question_text: Can one apply or develop bosonization, or bosonization-like constructions, that convert the graded and braided paraparticle Hopf structures into ordinary Hopf structures with trivial braiding while preserving equivalent representation theory?

evidence.quote: 3rd Research Objective: Apply or develop suitable bosonization or bosonization-like techniques to obtain ordinary Hopf structures, with no grading and with trivial braiding, possessing equivalent representation theories.

accepted.question_text: Can the braided-tensor-product method be completed to give explicit Fock-like representations of the infinite-degree-of-freedom parabosonic algebra PB? In particular, can one develop the needed multinomial theorem for the anticommuting creation operators that arise in the graded tensor-product realization, so that the action of PB generators and the corresponding matrix elements can be computed explicitly?

evidence.quote: We first intend to proceed to the explicit construction of the Fock-like representations in the case of the (inf. deg. of freedom) parabosonic PB and parafermionic PF algebra following the methodology developed in [103] and outlined above.

The mathematical problem here, which is necessary to be solved in order to explicitly perform the computation is the development of a suitable multinomial theorem in the anticommuting variables (b_i^{(k)+}).

accepted.question_text: When one decomposes the graded tensor-product representations built for PB and PF, do irreducible components appear beyond the known p-Fock-like modules? In other words, can these decompositions produce direct summands or more general submodules that are not equivalent to the standard p-Fock-like representations?

evidence.quote: In [103] we have proved that the p-Fock-like modules are contained as irreducible factors of such graded, tensor product representations. However, it remains to see whether such decompositions can produce as direct summands or more generally as submodules other non-equivalent representations as well.

accepted.question_text: Can the same braided-representation strategy be extended from PB and PF to the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB by viewing Ws and Was as suitable graded quotient algebras? To make that extension work, can one develop the required multinomial theorem that handles expressions mixing commuting and anticommuting variables?

evidence.quote: The next step will consist of generalizing the above calculations for the case of the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB. The philosophy of the method is based on the same idea: The Fock-like representations of PBF and PFB will be extracted as irreducible submodules arising in the decomposition of the graded tensor product representations of Ws and Was.
Finally it is worth mentioning, that the computational problem we expect to reveal here is the development of a suitable multinomial theorem mixing commuting and anticommuting variables.

accepted.question_text: Do the proposed paraparticle Hamiltonians built from a monochromatic parabosonic field and a (p + 1)-level system yield exactly solvable generalizations of the Jaynes-Cummings model? If so, can one compute their energy levels, eigenfunctions, and transition rates and compare those predictions directly with theoretical and experimental results?

evidence.quote: Using the Fock-like modules described above, we will attempt to proceed in a generalization of the above model in the study of the interaction of a monochromatic parabosonic field with a (p + 1)-level system.

In this way, we will actually construct a family of exactly solvable, quantum mechanical models, whose properties will be studied quantitatively (computation of energy levels, eigenfunctions, rates of transitions between states, etc.) and directly compared with theoretical and experimental results.
